label: conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit
title: Jet-filtered knot invariant converges to classical dimension-weighted average
html:
Conjecture. Jet-filtered knot invariant converges to classical dimension-weighted average

Conjecture (exact at k = 3, convergence at k > 3). At k = 3, the jet-filtered knot invariant evaluates exactly using the q-deformed Wedderburn weights W_\lambda = d_q(\lambda)^2 / [3]_q!. As the jet level k \to \infty, the invariant converges to the linear q-dimension scaling f_\mu^\infty = d_q(\mu)/\sum d_q(\nu).

The classical branching multiplicities remain q-independent, but the q-hook corrections do not factorize over the branching. The Kerov q-hook walk and the Féray-Méliot q-Plancherel Central Limit Theorem ensure O(1/\sqrt{k}) convergence. The q-deformation critically enhances the standard channel at low k, explaining why the nuclear topology dominates binding exclusively at physical energy scales.
